title: The hypertrophy series: multiplying tonnage accumulation using supersets
summary: NH argues supersets of different, non-interfering muscle groups give two muscular failures for the price of one without hurting performance, especially for arms, calves and back. He builds up to 'infinite' giant sets (his arm day runs five movements back to back), warns against supersetting the same muscle or compounds, and keeps strength work as solo sets.
claims: Supersets are underestimated as a bro tactic but are key for small, neglected muscles: arms, calves and parts of the back
Supersetting two different muscle groups does not impair performance; at most cardiovascular performance suffers
An 'infinite giant set' of more than four movements can cycle indefinitely without rest; the eventual drop comes from accumulated sets, not the superset
A superset never trains the same body part twice; that is pre-fatigue or a finisher, a different concept
Supersets give two muscular failures for the price of one, e.g. biceps then triceps which do not interfere
Getting winded, pumped or uncomfortable is not muscular failure
My arm day superset: biceps, shoulders, triceps, forearms, upper back, five movements back to back with rising performance
Build up gradually: start with two-exercise supersets, then trisets, then giant sets of four or more
Sitting two minutes after a calf set is stupid; do grippers or pull-ups in that time
Supersets avoid mechanical failure because successive lifts use different angles of the structure
Supersetting compounds is harder because they tax the cardio system and recruit many muscles; possible but be smart
Do strength work as solo sets to stay fresh and focused
Pair synergistic muscles; long-head triceps with calves is valid but not smart
